pins.definition: A set of written or printed pages bound together inside a cover.
A written or printed work consisting of pages bound together inside a cover.
A written work or set of printed pages fastened together inside a cover.

situation: A reader sitting at a heavy oak desk turns a page of a thick, cloth-bound volume.
subject: the bound pages
brief: A thick, cloth-bound volume lies open in the center of a dark oak desk, its cream-colored pages filled with dense lines of text and held firmly together by a stitched spine. The edges of the paper show the layered stack of hundreds of individual leaves pressed tightly between two hard covers. Warm lamplight catches the embossed texture of the cover fabric and the slight curl of the page currently being turned.
prompt: A thick, cloth-bound volume lies open in the center of a dark oak desk, its cream-colored pages filled with dense lines of text and held firmly together by a stitched spine. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
